T0.scene_summary: A pink-walled conference room with a long table, rolling chairs, checkerboard flooring, wall windows and a dark door.
T0.overall_evidence: The reconstruction captures the principal room colors, conference furniture, checkerboard floor and wall openings, but presents them from a much more distant elevated viewpoint. The door obstructs the center of the scene, and the table, chairs and surface finishes differ noticeably from the reference.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction uses a distant, elevated exterior-like view of an open room, rather than the reference's close interior view. The table and chairs consequently occupy much less of the image, with a large dark background visible around the room.
main_defects.evidence: The reference fills the frame with the room interior, while the reconstruction shows room boundaries and dark space above and around them.
main_defects.uncertainty: Some apparent differences in object scale and placement may be caused by the camera rather than scene geometry.

main_defects.description: The dark door stands across the center-right foreground and conceals a substantial part of the table and seating; in the reference it is confined to the far right edge.
main_defects.evidence: The reconstruction's tall dark slab overlaps the central furniture, whereas the reference door mostly frames the right side.
main_defects.uncertainty: The difference could be due partly to camera position or door angle.

main_defects.description: The table appears pale and plain rather than dark, streaked and highly reflective. The floor is a more uniform small-scale pink and gray checkerboard, missing much of the reference's mottled brown variation and strong reflections; the door also lacks visible panel detailing.
main_defects.evidence: The reference tabletop has pronounced dark wood-like streaks and bright reflections, and its floor shows varied brown tiles and window reflections; the reconstruction surfaces are comparatively flat and uniform.
main_defects.uncertainty: Lighting and the different viewing angle can affect apparent reflectivity and color.

main_defects.description: The visible chairs have boxier, straighter white backs than the reference's rounded, softly shaped beige seats and backs; their silhouettes appear simplified.
main_defects.evidence: The foreground reference chairs show curved, continuous upholstered forms and dark wheeled bases, while the reconstruction's visible chair backs are nearly rectangular.
main_defects.uncertainty: The reconstruction chairs are small in the frame and some are obscured by the door.

main_defects.description: The long multi-pane window occupies a smaller fraction of the visible left wall in the reconstruction and appears less prominent than in the reference.
main_defects.evidence: The reference window extends across most of the visible left wall, while the reconstruction shows a shorter-looking strip with more exposed wall around it.
main_defects.uncertainty: Perspective and the wider framing may account for part of the apparent size difference.

strengths: The pink walls and white baseboards are recognizable.
A long conference table surrounded by rolling chairs is present.
The floor has a pink and dark checkerboard pattern.
A long divided wall window, a smaller rear wall opening, a small plant and a dark door are represented.
T0.uncertainty: This is an initial automated visual judgment, not a human rating or validated aggregate metric. The images have substantially different viewpoints and framing, and the foreground door obscures parts of the reconstruction. Hidden geometry and exact object counts cannot be reliably assessed.

T1.scene_summary: A pink-walled conference room with a long table, rolling chairs, framed wall glazing, a checkerboard floor, and a dark door.
T1.overall_evidence: The reconstruction captures the principal room type, palette and furniture arrangement, but the elevated, distant view and centrally obstructing door substantially change the visible composition. The table, chairs, floor and door also lack several prominent material and shape details visible in the reference.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction is viewed from much farther away and higher up, showing a cutaway room against a dark background rather than the close, immersive interior view. The table and chairs consequently occupy much less of the image.
main_defects.evidence: The reference fills the frame with the room interior, while the reconstruction exposes exterior background above and around the room and a large foreground expanse of floor.
main_defects.uncertainty: The differing viewpoint affects apparent dimensions and occlusion, so it is difficult to isolate camera effects from actual scene layout differences.

main_defects.description: The dark door projects into the central foreground and blocks a substantial part of the table and seating, unlike the reference where it is mostly confined to the right edge.
main_defects.evidence: A tall black slab crosses the right-center of the reconstruction and hides the far portion of the table; the reference door frames the scene on the extreme right.
main_defects.uncertainty: The difference may arise partly from camera placement or door angle rather than door location alone.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction simplifies the reference's glossy, streaked wood table, varied dark wood-toned reflective checkerboard floor, and paneled dark teal door into comparatively flat pale, regular pink-gray, and nearly black surfaces.
main_defects.evidence: The reference tabletop has strong lengthwise wood-like streaks and highlights; its floor tiles vary in brown tone and reflection. The reconstruction table is nearly uniform, its checker pattern is more uniform, and the door face lacks visible panel detail.
main_defects.uncertainty: Some apparent texture and reflectivity differences could be amplified by the different view, resolution, and lighting.

main_defects.description: The visible chair backs are boxier and more upright than the reference's rounded, gently curved upholstered shells; the seating silhouettes are correspondingly simplified.
main_defects.evidence: Several foreground reference chairs have rounded tapering backs and distinct curved seats, while the reconstructed foreground chairs have largely rectangular slab-like backs.
main_defects.uncertainty: The smaller scale of the reconstructed chairs obscures fine details and some chairs are hidden by the door.

main_defects.description: The long framed glazing on the left wall appears shorter and smaller relative to the surrounding wall, and the back-wall opening is also much less prominent.
main_defects.evidence: The reference left glazing spans most of the visible left wall and is a dominant feature; the corresponding reconstruction frame occupies a smaller section of the wall, while the back frame is partly concealed.
main_defects.uncertainty: Perspective, room framing, and the obstructing door affect the apparent sizes; the true physical dimensions cannot be established from these views.

strengths: The reconstruction clearly depicts a conference room with a long rectangular table and multiple light-colored wheeled chairs arranged around it.
Pink walls, white baseboards, a checkerboard floor, long subdivided left-wall glazing, and a framed opening on the back wall are recognizable correspondences.
A dark door-like element and a small green plant near the far end of the table are present.
T1.uncertainty: This is an initial automated visual judgment, not a human rating or validated aggregate metric. The images use substantially different viewpoints and scales, and the door occludes parts of the reconstruction; hidden objects and geometry cannot be reliably assessed.
